section_1_why_are_we_here.current_state: Newsletter creation is a manual, time-consuming process requiring hours of research, writing, and assembly. Educators struggle to maintain consistent publication schedules while managing other responsibilities.
consequences: Newsletters take hours or days to create, limiting educator productivity
Reduced newsletter frequency or quality due to time constraints
Educators unable to focus on other important educational activities
Potential for topic repetition without systematic tracking
section_1_why_are_we_here.success_vision: AshlarPress enables educators to assemble inspiring newsletters in a few hours instead of days, with AI-assisted content gathering that sparks curiosity and encourages readers to explore topics further.
success_criteria: Ability to build a full year of newsletters (12+ issues)
Reduce assembly time to a few hours per issue
Human review and editing remains part of the workflow
All content includes proper source citations
No unintentional topic repetition across issues
Content inspires readers to explore topics further

key_drivers.rationale: Reduce newsletter creation from hours/days to a few hours
AI-gathered content with citations that inspires further research
Editors remain at the center of research and editorial decisions

section_3_product_box.product_description: AshlarPress is a newsletter generation engine that gathers, cites, and organizes content from configurable sources. It uses AI agents for research, copywriting, and image generation while keeping human editors in control.

key_benefits.detail: Reduce newsletter assembly from hours/days to a few hours
All gathered content includes source attribution for verification
Content designed to encourage readers to explore topics further

technical_highlights: YAML-based configuration for sections, prompts, and exclusions
Configurable AI CLI backends (Claude, Gemini, Copilot)
Mustache templating for consistent newsletter formatting
Topic Ledger for cross-issue topic tracking
requirements: AI CLI tool with valid license (Claude CLI, Gemini CLI, or Copilot CLI)
section_3_product_box.testimonial_quote: AshlarPress transformed our monthly newsletter from a dreaded chore into an enjoyable curation experience.
section_3_product_box.call_to_action: Clone the repository and start creating your first newsletter in minutes.

section_6_show_solution.solution_overview: AshlarPress is an orchestration layer that coordinates AI agents (Research, Copywriter, Image) via configurable AI CLI tools, assembles their output with human contributions, and renders newsletters using Mustache templates.
section_6_show_solution.solution_diagram_description: High-level architecture showing config, agent orchestration, assembly engine, and output rendering

components.name: Config (YAML)
components.purpose: Defines sections, prompts, exclusion sites, agent CLI assignments

components.name: Agent Orchestrator
components.purpose: Coordinates fan-out to Research, Copywriter, Image agents
components.interactions: Invokes AI CLI tools, collects output

components.name: Research Agent
components.purpose: Gathers content from web, cites sources, respects exclusions

components.name: Copywriter Agent
components.interactions: Receives gathered content, outputs refined copy

components.name: Image Agent
components.purpose: Generates visuals aligned to copy context

components.name: Editor Contributions
components.interactions: Read by Assembly Engine, classified to sections

components.name: Assembly Engine
components.purpose: Merges content, applies templates, checks ledger, renders output
components.interactions: Reads all content, writes issue.json, renders MD/PDF/HTML

components.name: Topic Ledger
components.purpose: Master list preventing topic repetition across issues

steps.description: Editor configures newsletter.yaml (sections, prompts, exclusions, agent assignments)
Editor optionally drops contributions into input/contributions/
Editor runs AshlarPress for a specific issue
System processes contributions first, classifies to sections
System performs gap analysis to identify sections needing content
Agents gather, write, and generate images for gaps
Assembly Engine merges all content into issue.json
Editor reviews and edits the Markdown
Topic Ledger updated with covered topics

section_6_show_solution.architecture_style: Local-first CLI orchestration with pluggable AI backends

technologies.rationale: Developer preference, good CLI tooling support
Structured data for issue.json and Topic Ledger

section_6_show_solution.data_flow_description: 1. Human contributions processed first and classified. 2. Gap analysis identifies needed content. 3. Agents fill gaps. 4. All contributions (human + agent) compiled into issue.json. 5. Mustache renders from issue.json. 6. PDF/HTML generated from Markdown.
section_6_show_solution.data_flow_diagram:
Contributions → Classify → issue.json ← Agents
                              ↓
                    Mustache Template
                              ↓
                    newsletter.md
                              ↓
                    newsletter.pdf / .html
section_6_show_solution.deployment_model: Local-first: runs on editor's machine via VSCode terminal

risks.title: AI CLI tool changes/breaks
risks.description: AI CLI tools (Claude, Gemini, Copilot) may change their interfaces or become unavailable
risks.likelihood_rationale: CLI tools are actively developed and may change
risks.impact_rationale: Core functionality depends on CLI tools
risks.mitigation: Abstract CLI calls behind interface; support multiple providers

risks.title: LLM hallucinations / bad sources
risks.description: AI agents may produce inaccurate content or cite unreliable sources
risks.likelihood_rationale: LLMs can hallucinate; this is a known limitation
risks.impact_rationale: Bad content could damage newsletter credibility
risks.mitigation: Human editor review required; all sources cited for verification
risks.contingency: Editor rejects and manually researches section

risks.title: API costs escalate
risks.description: Frequent use of AI agents could result in higher than expected API costs
risks.impact_rationale: Could limit usage or require cost optimization
risks.mitigation: Configurable model selection; use cheaper models where appropriate; monitor token usage
risks.contingency: Reduce agent usage; use more human contributions

risks.title: Scope creep
risks.description: Feature requests may expand scope beyond manageable levels
risks.mitigation: Strong NOT List; prioritize core workflow first; phased delivery
